draft.title: Repeatability and reproducibility
card: the same person, using the same method and equipment, gets close to the same results when the investigation is repeated.
different people, or a different method or equipment, get close to the same results.
Repeating trials helps show whether results are repeatable. It also helps spot a result that does not fit.
Results that other groups can reproduce are more trustworthy, because a one-off result might come from something unusual in one setup.
draft.remember: Repeatable: same person, same method. Reproducible: different people or methods.

a.q: Sam measures the heat released by burning ethanol three times with the same set-up and gets very similar results. What has Sam shown?
a.why: The same person repeated the same method and got similar results, so they are repeatable. Reproducibility would need another person or method. Similar results do not show they are close to a true value.
a.clue: Who did the repeating, and which method did they use?

b.q: A school group finds the mass of copper formed in a reaction. A group at another school follows the same method and gets a similar mass. What does this show?
b.why: A different group of people got a similar result, so the result is reproducible. Repeatable would describe the same group repeating it. Agreement between groups does not prove accuracy.
b.clue: Was it the same people or different people?

problems.detail: Why (a) explains accuracy ('close to a true value'), a term that belongs to point 2 (accuracy, precision and validity), instead of only mentioning it.

proposal.title: Repeatability and reproducibility
card: the same person, using the same method and equipment, gets close to the same results when the investigation is repeated.
different people, or a different method or equipment, get close to the same results.
Repeating trials helps show whether results are repeatable. It also helps spot a result that does not fit.
Results that other groups can reproduce are more trustworthy, because a one-off result might come from something unusual in one setup.
proposal.remember: Repeatable: same person, same method. Reproducible: different people or methods.

a.q: Sam measures the heat released by burning ethanol three times with the same set-up and gets very similar results. What has Sam shown?
opts: The results are repeatable and reproducible
The results are neither repeatable nor reproducible
a.why: The same person repeated the same method and got similar results, so they are repeatable. Reproducible would need a different person, method or equipment to get similar results, and nobody else has tried yet.
a.clue: Who did the repeating, and which method did they use?

b.q: A school group finds the mass of copper formed in a reaction. A group at another school follows the same method and gets a similar mass. What does this show?
opts: The result came from one unusual setup
b.why: A different group of people got a similar result, so the result is reproducible. Repeatable would describe the first group repeating it themselves. Because two separate setups agreed, the result is unlikely to come from something unusual in one setup.
b.clue: Was it the same people or different people?
